title: Word Passes the Rules
statement:
A form accepts a word only if it passes all four rules:

  • It has at least 3 characters.
  • Every character is an English letter (either case) or a digit 0–9.
  • It contains at least one vowel: a, e, i, o, u in either case.
  • It contains at least one consonant: any English letter that is not a vowel. Digits are neither vowels nor consonants, and y counts as a consonant.

Given word, return true if it passes, otherwise false. The input may contain the symbols @, # and $, which are never allowed.

examples.why: Five characters, only letters and a digit, has the vowel i and consonants P, x, l.
Two vowels and a digit, but no consonant. A digit does not count as one.
Long enough and all letters, but y is a consonant here, so there is no vowel.

constraints: word consists of English letters, digits, '@', '#' and '$'
hints: Check each rule separately. Which one can you decide without looking at the characters at all?
Walk the string once and keep two flags: seen a vowel, seen a consonant. Return false at once on a forbidden character.
A character is a consonant if it is a letter and not in the vowel set. Lowercase it before checking so 'E' and 'e' behave the same.

explain.intuition:
This is form validation, the kind you write for a sign-up field. The trap is in the definitions, not the algorithm: a digit is allowed but is neither a vowel nor a consonant, and y is a consonant.

One pass with two flags is enough. Check the length first, reject any character that is not a letter or digit, and at the end require both flags to be set.
steps: For each character: if it is a digit, continue. If it is not a letter, return false.
If its lowercase form is in aeiou, mark a vowel seen; otherwise mark a consonant seen.
Return whether both a vowel and a consonant were seen.
pitfalls: Counting digits as consonants because they are "not vowels". "a1e" must be false.
Checking vowels in lowercase only, so "BOX" looks like it has no vowel.
Testing the character class with a regex like \w, which also accepts _.

solutions.title: One pass with two flags
solutions.idea: Reject short words and forbidden characters, then require at least one vowel and one consonant.

followups: Return the list of rules a word breaks, so the form can show every error at once.
Make the rules configurable (minimum length, allowed symbols) without rewriting the loop.
